title: Electrostatic effects in nano-reactor-confined charge regulated macroions
authors: Manit Klawtanong, Petch Khunpetch, Huaqiong Li, Shigeyuki Komura
abstract: We formulate a thermodynamic model of a nano-reactor containing charge-regulated macroions within an electrolyte-permeable enclosure. The model is then formalized within the Poisson-Boltzmann electrostatics augmented by the consistent inclusion of the charge dissociation of molecular groups residing on the surface of the entrapped macroions via charge regulation formalism. By solving the basic equilibrium equations in the linearized Debye-Hückel type approximation, we analyze the salient features of the inhomogeneous electrolyte distribution and macroion charge. We found that the surface charge asymmetry/symmetry of the macroions strongly affects the spatial profile of electrostatic potential. The effective screening length shows the non-monotonic behavior, arising from the complex interplay between the bathing external solution and macroion effective charges, which govern charge regulation equilibria. The total pressure at the nano-reactor enclosure boundary decreases monotonically as the enclosure radius and the ionic bulk salt concentration increase. Also, the resulting pressure is strongly influenced by the surface charge densities of the nano-reactor and the number of confined macroions.
summary: This paper develops a thermodynamic model describing macroions confined in a nano-reactor immersed in an electrolyte solution. By coupling Poisson-Boltzmann theory with charge regulation formalism, the authors analyze how surface charge asymmetry affects the potential profile and effective screening length. Key findings show that pressure decreases monotonically with increasing reactor size or salt concentration, providing insights into nanoscale electrostatics.
main_problem: The study formulates a thermodynamic model for macroions confined within a nano-reactor, focusing on how charge regulation equilibria influence the electrostatic potential and pressure.
main_result: Surface charge asymmetry strongly dictates the spatial profile of the electrostatic potential, and the effective screening length exhibits non-monotonic behavior due to complex interplay between external solution and macroion charges.
method: The analysis uses a thermodynamic framework minimizing a free energy functional, solved via linearized Debye-Hückel type approximations applied to Poisson-Boltzmann Charge Regulation (PB-CR) equations.
model_or_system: The system is an electrolyte-permeable nano-reactor containing charge-regulated macroions. The model combines grand canonical ensembles for mobile ions with a fixed number of confined macroions, incorporating Langmuir isotherm descriptions for surface adsorption/desorption equilibria.
key_observables: Electrostatic potential profile ($\psi(r)$), ionic density distributions ($n_\pm$), total pressure at the enclosure boundary, and effective screening length ($\lambda_{eff}$).
important_parameters: Enclosure radius ($R$), bulk salt concentration ($n_0$), surface charge densities ($\sigma_R$, $\sigma_{R+w}$), and the number of confined macroions ($N_p$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linearizing the full non-linear PB-CR equations (Debye-Hückel approximation) and assumes that the macroion cargo is fixed in number rather than being in bulk equilibrium.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate scaled electrostatic potential profiles ($ eta_e\psi(r)$) for varying numbers of macroions, spatial charge density distributions showing asymmetry effects, and plots demonstrating monotonic pressure decrease with increasing radius or salt concentration.
paper_structure: The paper develops the free energy functional incorporating charge regulation, linearizes the resulting coupled differential equations (PB-CR), solves for radial profiles in different regions (inside/wall/outside), and analyzes key observables like potential, screening length, and pressure dependence on system parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding confined electrochemistry where surface chemistry (charge regulation) dictates macroscopic properties like osmotic pressure and electrostatic screening, relevant to biomolecular confinement.
